q: 准备 AI 编码面试最有效的一件事是什么？
q_en: What is the most effective way to prepare for an AI coding interview?
scenario: 距离 AI 编码面试还有两周，每周只挤得出 5 小时，你从没在限时压力下用 AI 做完一整题。
scenario_en: Your AI coding interview is two weeks out, you have about five hours a week, and you've never finished a whole problem with AI under a clock.
options: 反复读面经帖总结的解题思路，但没有掐表完整做完一整道题
找一道真实题目，按面试时长完整做完并拿到反馈
把几套万能提示词模板背熟，面试时不管题目直接照搬
反复看别人比赛解题的录屏，自己全程不动手写代码
options_en: Repeatedly reading conclusions from interview-experience posts, but never actually finishing a full problem against the clock.
Pick a real problem, finish it under real interview time, and get feedback on it.
Memorize several go-to prompt templates and blindly reuse them in the interview no matter the problem.
Repeatedly watch other people's competition/solve recordings without ever writing any code yourself.
why: 唯一能同时练到问题拆解、AI 驱动、验证和沟通四项能力的，是完整做题并拿到反馈；反馈能精确指出面试前该补哪一项。
why_en: Full practice with feedback works best because it trains problem breakdown, AI control, verification, and communication together, then points at what to fix.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Practice[Full practice] --> Record[Capture prompts]
  Record --> Feedback[Get feedback]
  Feedback --> Fix[Pick one weakness]
  Fix --> Practice

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

optionExplanations: 只读经验帖等于把准备停在别人的总结上，你自己还没在压力下真正驱动过 AI、验证过代码。
把一整套流程走一遍——限时、动手写、拿反馈——比任何被动学习更能让你看清自己哪里薄弱。
背熟话术容易让你误以为准备好了，可换一个陌生代码库，固定模板立刻就露馅。
看别人操作会让你误以为自己也会了，其实旁观学不到自己动手时才会暴露的判断和失误。
optionExplanations_en: Only reading experience posts keeps you at someone else's summary — you still haven't driven AI or verified code under real pressure yourself.
Running the whole loop yourself — timed, hands-on, then reviewed — exposes your real weak spots far better than any passive reading can.
Memorizing a script can feel like readiness, but it falls apart the moment you hit an unfamiliar codebase that doesn't match the template.
Watching someone else solve it can feel like learning, but it skips the judgment calls and mistakes you only hit by doing it yourself.

scenario: AI 编码面试练习平台把练习分成两条通道：一条给你 clone 仓库到本地写代码，另一条直接在浏览器沙盒里用平台自带 AI 分阶段出题。
scenario_en: An AI coding interview practice platform offers two tracks: one has you clone a repo and code locally, while the other puts you in a browser sandbox with the platform's built-in AI and staged prompts.
q: 这两条练习通道分别复刻了哪两类真实面试现场？
q_en: Which two real interview settings do these practice tracks recreate?
options: 两条通道其实都只是同一种纯电话面试，没有实质差别
开放式对应在线算法笔试网站，结构化对应系统设计白板画图
开放式对应 BYOE 面试，结构化对应内置 AI 面试
开放式对应现场白板面试，结构化对应邮件异步文字面试
options_en: Both tracks are really just the same plain phone screen, with no real difference.
Open-ended corresponds to online algorithm quiz sites, structured corresponds to system-design whiteboard diagramming.
Open-ended corresponds to BYOE interviews, structured corresponds to interviews with built-in AI.
Open-ended corresponds to in-person whiteboard interviews, structured corresponds to async written email interviews.
why: 开放式通道复刻用自己编辑器、AI 工具屏幕共享的面试；结构化通道复刻 CoderPad/HackerRank 式内置 AI 的分阶段面试。
why_en: The open-ended track mirrors BYOE screen-share interviews with your own tools, while the structured track mirrors phased CoderPad/HackerRank-style interviews with built-in AI.
tradeoff: 复刻自带工具的 BYOE 面试 vs 复刻平台内置 AI 的结构化面试

termDefinitions.meaning: 候选人自带日常使用的编辑器和 AI 工具、屏幕共享作答的开放式面试形式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BYOE means the candidate brings their own editor and AI tools and screen-shares while working.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款常见的在线协作编程面试平台，内置浏览器代码编辑器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CoderPad is a common online collaborative coding interview platform with a built-in browser editor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 另一款常用的在线编程测评/面试平台，题目按阶段推进。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HackerRank is another common online coding assessment platform that advances problems in stages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

optionExplanations: 把两条通道都归为同一种电话面试，抹平了工具来源上的真实差别。
算法笔试网站不用 AI 助手、系统设计画图不写代码，两边都对不上这两条练习通道。
两条通道分别照着你会遇到的真实工具来源设计，选对了就能提前适应当天节奏。
白板面试和异步邮件都不涉及实时 AI 协作，套错了这两条通道想复刻的场景。
optionExplanations_en: Lumping both tracks into one plain phone screen erases the real difference in who provides the tools.
Algorithm-quiz sites skip AI assistance and whiteboarding skips coding, so neither actually matches these two tracks.
Each track is built around the real tool source you'll face, so picking correctly means the pacing won't feel unfamiliar on the day.
Whiteboard and async email interviews involve no live AI collaboration, so they don't match what these tracks recreate.

scenario: 你的目标公司允许使用自己的 IDE 和日常 AI 工具，并让你屏幕共享从仓库开始构建。
scenario_en: Your target company lets you use your own IDE and daily AI tools while screen-sharing as you build from a repo.
q: 该优先练哪种练习方式？
q_en: Which practice format should you prioritize?
options: 先在结构化浏览器沙盒里适应平台内置 AI 的分阶段流程
只精读该公司过往面试真题，不动手写代码
用在线协作文档写下解题思路，但不实际提交可运行代码
clone 仓库计时完成，用自己工具独立提交反馈
options_en: Warm up in a structured browser sandbox to get used to the platform's built-in AI and its staged flow.
Only re-read this company's past interview questions without writing any code.
Write your approach in a shared doc, but never actually submit runnable code.
Clone the repo, time yourself, finish independently with your own tools, and submit for feedback.
why: 目标公司走 BYOE 屏幕共享，练习就该照搬你会用到的编辑器、AI 工具和真实计时，而不是先去适应平台沙盒。
why_en: Because the target interview is BYOE screen-share, you should practice with your own editor, AI tools, and real timing instead of a platform sandbox.
whenOtherWins: 如果目标公司明确使用 CoderPad 或 HackerRank，结构化沙盒反而更贴近当天体验。
tradeoff: 复刻自己工具的真实工作流 vs 提前适应平台内置沙盒

termDefinitions.meaning: 候选人自带日常使用的编辑器和 AI 工具、屏幕共享作答的开放式面试形式。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: BYOE means the candidate brings their own editor and AI tools and screen-shares while working.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集成开发环境，也就是你日常写代码用的编辑器软件，例如 VS Code。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An IDE is the integrated development environment, the editor software you normally write code in, like VS Code.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款常见的在线协作编程面试平台，内置浏览器代码编辑器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CoderPad is a common online collaborative coding interview platform with a built-in browser editor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 另一款常用的在线编程测评/面试平台，题目按阶段推进。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HackerRank is another common online coding assessment platform that advances problems in stages.

optionExplanations: 如果目标真的换成 CoderPad/HackerRank 类平台轮，这条路才对；眼下场景是 BYOE，练错了工具来源。
只读题不写代码，练不出用自己工具驱动 AI、边写边验证的手感，到了真实屏幕共享会露怯。
记思路不提交可运行代码，最后连自己有没有理解实现都验证不了，更别说拿到有依据的反馈。
复刻你当天真正会打开的那套开发环境和限时节奏，练出来的手感能直接带进 BYOE 面试。
optionExplanations_en: This fits if the target flips to a CoderPad/HackerRank-style round, but here the interview is BYOE, so it drills the wrong tool source.
Reading without writing code never builds the feel of driving AI and verifying output with your own tools under a real screen-share.
Jotting an approach without submitting runnable code leaves nothing to verify your understanding against, let alone grounded feedback.
Recreating the exact toolchain and time limit you'll actually use on the day carries straight into the real BYOE interview.

scenario: 你的目标面试会在 CoderPad 或 HackerRank 里进行，AI 助手是平台内置的。
scenario_en: Your target interview will happen in CoderPad or HackerRank, with the AI assistant built into the platform.
q: 最该优先练什么？
q_en: What should you practice first?
options: 在结构化浏览器沙盒里，跟着平台内置 AI 走完分阶段题目
只在本地 Cursor 里用惯用快捷键反复练手，不碰浏览器沙盒
提前把公司官网介绍、产品线和团队成员背得滚瓜烂熟
只反复用系统设计画图工具练架构图，全程不写一行代码
options_en: Work through the structured browser sandbox with the platform's built-in AI across staged problems.
Just keep practicing with your usual hotkeys in local Cursor, without touching the browser sandbox.
Memorize the company's website bio, product lines, and team members by heart ahead of time.
Only drill system-design diagramming tools repeatedly, without writing a single line of code.
why: 结构化沙盒和 CoderPad/HackerRank 平台内置 AI 高度相似，提前适应能减少正式面试当天的工具摩擦。
why_en: Since the interview runs on CoderPad or HackerRank with built-in AI, practicing the structured sandbox now removes tool friction on the real day.
whenOtherWins: 如果目标轮其实是开放式屏幕共享，先打磨自己本地编辑器和日常 AI 工具更贴近当天。
tradeoff: 提前适应平台内置沙盒 vs 打磨自己本地编辑器工作流

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款常见的在线协作编程面试平台，内置浏览器代码编辑器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CoderPad is a common online collaborative coding interview platform with a built-in browser editor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 另一款常用的在线编程测评/面试平台，题目按阶段推进。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HackerRank is another common online coding assessment platform that advances problems in stages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款内置 AI 辅助的本地代码编辑器产品。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: Cursor is a local code editor product with built-in AI assistance.

optionExplanations: 分阶段推进和内置 AI 的限制提前练熟，正式面试当天工具就不会抢注意力。
本地 Cursor 的快捷键在受限浏览器沙盒里大概率用不上，练错了当天真正要用的环境。
背公司资料不会让你更快适应受限编辑器和分阶段节奏，这轮考的是手上功夫。
这轮是编码面试不是系统设计画图，只练画图完全绕开了要考的能力。
optionExplanations_en: Getting used to the staged flow and the constrained built-in AI ahead of time means the tools won't steal attention on the real day.
Local Cursor hotkeys mostly won't carry into a locked-down browser sandbox, so it drills the wrong environment for this round.
Memorizing company facts doesn't help you adapt faster to a constrained editor and staged pacing — this round tests hands-on skill.
This round is a coding interview, not system-design diagramming, so drilling diagrams sidesteps what's actually being evaluated.

q: 补全开放式练习流程：
q_en: Complete the open-ended practice flow:
text: 开放式练习会给你 clone repo 的命令，配合真实面试长度的{{计时器}}；完成后上传{{代码}}和{{AI 聊天}}获得反馈。
why: 这个流程刻意复刻真实工作流，让计时和反馈都对着你真实会用到的代码与 AI 交互记录。
why_en: Open-ended practice times you realistically and reviews both your code and your AI chat log, just like the real interview.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Pick[Pick problem] --> Timer[Start timer]
  Timer --> Build[Build with AI]
  Build --> Test[Test]
  Test --> Review[Review transcript]

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

termDefinitions.meaning: 代码仓库，通常用 git clone 命令下载到本地。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: A repo is a code repository, usually downloaded locally with the git clone command.

scenario: 在开放式练习里，你 clone 仓库到本地，用日常工具完整做完一题后提交成果。
scenario_en: In open-ended practice, you clone the repo locally, solve the problem with your daily tools, and submit the result.
q: 系统给出的反馈通常基于哪些材料？（多选）
q_en: What materials does the system usually use for feedback? (Select all that apply.)
options: 你提交的代码
你和 AI 的聊天记录
hire/no-hire 评级和具体改进建议
你对目标薪资的期望
options_en: The code you submitted.
Your chat transcript with the AI.
A hire/no-hire rating plus concrete suggestions for improvement.
Your target salary expectations.
why: 反馈要同时评估成品和过程，尤其是你是否在聊天记录里体现了对 AI 的控制力，而不只是最终代码能不能跑。
why_en: Feedback covers both the final code and the AI chat log because reviewers check whether you stayed in control of the AI, not just whether the code runs.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

optionExplanations: 代码是评审能直接检查的成品，边界处理、实现质量都能从这里看出来。
聊天记录能看出你是在主导 AI 还是被 AI 牵着走，这是代码本身看不出来的过程证据。
评级加具体建议把反馈从对错判断变成下一轮该改什么的行动项。
薪资期望和你写代码、驱动 AI 的能力没有关系，混进来只会稀释真正有用的反馈。
optionExplanations_en: The code is the finished artifact reviewers can inspect directly for implementation quality and edge-case handling.
The chat log shows whether you were steering the AI or being steered, a piece of process evidence the code alone can't reveal.
A rating plus concrete suggestions turns the review from a pass/fail judgment into an actionable next step.
Salary expectations have nothing to do with your coding or AI-driving skill, and including them only dilutes the useful feedback.

scenario: Meta、LinkedIn、Uber 这类公司常把 AI 编码面试放进 CoderPad/HackerRank 式的浏览器沙盒里进行。
scenario_en: Companies like Meta, LinkedIn, and Uber often run AI coding interviews in CoderPad/HackerRank-style browser sandboxes.
q: 为什么建议提前练习这类结构化浏览器环境？
q_en: Why should you practice this kind of structured browser environment in advance?
options: 因为提前练好之后，就能完全跳过和面试官的沟通环节
让受限内置 AI、陌生编辑器和分阶段流程变熟悉
因为结构化题目从设计上就不会包含任何真实边界条件
因为平台内置 AI 会自动帮你补全并跑完所有测试用例
options_en: Because once you've practiced enough, you can skip talking to the interviewer entirely.
It makes the constrained built-in AI, unfamiliar editor, and staged flow feel familiar.
Because structured problems are designed to never include any real edge cases.
Because the platform's built-in AI automatically fills in and runs all your test cases for you.
why: CoderPad/HackerRank 这类平台体验和日常 IDE 差异很大，提前适应能把当天注意力留给题目而不是工具。
why_en: Practicing the structured sandbox in advance makes the constrained built-in AI and staged flow feel normal, so real interview attention goes to the problem, not the tool.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款常见的在线协作编程面试平台，内置浏览器代码编辑器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CoderPad is a common online collaborative coding interview platform with a built-in browser editor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 另一款常用的在线编程测评/面试平台，题目按阶段推进。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HackerRank is another common online coding assessment platform that advances problems in stages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集成开发环境，也就是你日常写代码用的编辑器软件，例如 VS Code。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An IDE is the integrated development environment, the editor software you normally write code in, like VS Code.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

optionExplanations: 沟通仍然是评估的四个维度之一，提前练平台环境跟能否跳过沟通没有关系。
陌生编辑器和受限 AI 会占用大量注意力，提前把这些摩擦点走顺，正式面试才能把心思留给题目本身。
结构化题目照样有边界条件要处理，不会因为换了平台就消失。
补测试用例仍然要你自己写和跑，平台不会替你把这一步做掉。
optionExplanations_en: Communication is still one of the four evaluated areas, and practicing the platform environment has nothing to do with skipping it.
An unfamiliar editor and constrained AI eat a lot of attention, so ironing out that friction beforehand frees your focus for the actual problem.
Structured problems still come with edge cases to handle — switching platforms doesn't make them go away.
You still have to write and run your own test cases; the platform won't do that step for you.

q: 把一次高质量练习闭环排好：
q_en: Put a high-quality practice loop in the right order:
steps: 根据反馈修正下次练习策略
选择与目标面试格式匹配的问题
上传代码和 AI 聊天获得评价
why: 练习要先挑对目标格式的题，在真实时限下完成，再靠反馈调整下一轮；只刷题不看反馈很难自我校准。
why_en: A useful practice loop matches the target format, runs under real time pressure, and then uses feedback to adjust the next attempt.
tradeoff: 先选对格式再计时完成 vs 不分格式无差别刷题
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Attempt[Timed attempt] --> Artifacts[Save code prompts]
  Artifacts --> Feedback[Review feedback]
  Feedback --> Drill[Drill weakness]
  Drill --> Next[Next attempt]

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

scenario: 你还不确定目标公司到底是开放式还是结构化 AI 面试。
scenario_en: You are not sure whether the target company uses an open-ended or structured AI interview.
q: 准备策略最稳的选择是什么？
q_en: What is the safest preparation strategy?
options: 只练你更熟悉的本地环境，赌面试是开放式
只练结构化浏览器沙盒，赌面试是平台面试
两种格式都至少完整练一次，降低猜错的风险
完全不做任何练习，等到面试当天临场应变
options_en: Only practice your familiar local setup and bet the interview is open-ended.
Only practice the structured browser sandbox and bet it's a platform interview.
Do at least one full practice run in both formats to cut the risk of guessing wrong.
Skip practice entirely and improvise on interview day.
why: 格式不确定时，两边都至少练一次能把猜错格式的风险降到最低，代价是要多花一次练习的时间。
why_en: When the target format is unknown, practicing both at least once minimizes the risk of guessing the wrong environment, at the cost of extra practice time.
whenOtherWins: 如果 recruiter 已经明确格式，就该把主要时间集中在对应环境上，不必平均分配。
tradeoff: 两边都练降低猜错风险 vs 押注一边省练习时间
optionExplanations: 格式确定是开放式时这个赌注就赢了，但眼下没人告诉你答案，猜错就当场吃工具摩擦。
格式确定是结构化平台时这个赌注才划算，猜错的话本地手感反而生疏了。
两边各花一次练习时间换来的是不管落在哪种格式，工具都已经摸过一遍。
两种环境都没碰过，当天不管遇到哪一种都要现场从头适应。
optionExplanations_en: This bet pays off only if the format really is open-ended; guess wrong and you eat tool friction live on the day.
This bet pays off only if the format really is a structured platform round; guess wrong and your local setup ends up rusty instead.
Spending one extra practice run on each format buys certainty — whichever one it turns out to be, the tools are already rehearsed.
Skipping both leaves you adapting to an unfamiliar environment from scratch, no matter which format shows up.

scenario: 你刚开始准备 AI 编码面试，还没熟悉双线沟通和 AI 验证节奏。
scenario_en: You are just starting AI coding interview prep and are not yet used to the rhythm of dual communication and AI verification.
q: 第一轮练习更适合怎么选题？
q_en: How should you choose a problem for your first practice round?
options: 一上来就直接选列表里最难的一题，硬扛计时和分阶段流程模拟最大压力
只反复读题目描述和示例，从不实际提交可运行代码
只反复看别人的解题录屏，自己完全不动手敲代码
先从 Easy 或熟悉的 Medium 起步，跑顺流程
options_en: Jump straight to the hardest problem on the list and force your way through the timer and staged flow to simulate max pressure.
Keep re-reading the problem statement and examples without ever submitting runnable code.
Keep rewatching other people's solve recordings without ever typing any code yourself.
Start with Easy or a familiar Medium problem and get the workflow smooth.
why: 早期要先把环境、计时、AI 使用和反馈这套流程跑顺，而不是一上来就用最大难度考验自己。
why_en: Early practice should get the full workflow smooth on an easier problem before you push straight to maximum difficulty.
whenOtherWins: 如果流程已经熟悉、目标公司题目又偏难，可以尽快切到 Hard 模拟真实压力。
tradeoff: 先跑顺流程再加难度 vs 一开始就上强度

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

optionExplanations: 流程还没跑顺时上最大难度，多个短板会一起爆发，反而看不清问题出在哪一环。
不写代码就练不到驱动 AI 和验证输出的手感，这两项恰恰是评估的核心。
旁观学不到自己动手时才会暴露的判断失误，这类练习攒不出真实经验。
先在简单题上把计时、AI 协作和反馈这套流程走顺，后面加难度时才不会手忙脚乱。
optionExplanations_en: Jumping to max difficulty before the workflow is smooth makes several gaps surface at once, so it's hard to tell what actually broke.
Skipping code writing means no practice driving AI or verifying its output, exactly the two skills this round evaluates.
Watching can't teach the judgment calls and mistakes that only show up once you're the one typing.
Getting the timer, AI collaboration, and feedback loop smooth on an easy problem first means adding difficulty later won't overwhelm you.

scenario: 你下周面试，目标轮据说会有多阶段和较强优化要求。
scenario_en: Your interview is next week, and the target round is said to include multiple stages and strong optimization requirements.
q: 更合理的练习组合是什么？
q_en: What is a more reasonable practice mix?
options: 只挑最简单的题反复刷，只求熟悉页面操作
至少做一个结构化 Medium，再做一个 Hard 模拟压力
完全不设置计时器，按自己节奏慢慢打磨代码
只刷传统 LeetCode 式 Easy 题，不碰浏览器沙盒
options_en: Only grind the easiest problems, just to get familiar with the page layout.
Do at least one structured Medium, then one Hard to simulate real pressure.
Skip the timer entirely and polish the code at your own pace.
Only grind traditional LeetCode-style Easy problems and skip the browser sandbox.
why: Medium 练节奏，Hard 练优化和复杂约束下的 AI 驱动，两个难度暴露的短板不同，缺一个都补不全。
why_en: A Medium problem builds rhythm while a Hard problem exposes optimization and constraint-handling gaps that a Medium alone won't surface.
whenOtherWins: 如果面试明确是开放式 BYOE，应把同样两档难度放到本地工具链里练，而不是浏览器沙盒。
tradeoff: 覆盖 Medium+Hard 两档暴露不同短板 vs 只练单一难度省时间

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个常见的算法刷题网站，题目多是单函数、无 AI 辅助。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LeetCode is a common algorithm-practice site with single-function problems and no AI assistance.

optionExplanations: 只在简单题上熟悉页面操作，练不到多阶段推进和优化要求实际需要的能力。
Medium 先把节奏跑顺，Hard 再逼出优化思路，两档难度合起来才对上这轮的要求。
去掉计时器等于放弃了正式面试最大的资源约束，正式当天的节奏依然是陌生的。
传统 Easy 题是单函数、没有分阶段推进，练的是完全不同的一套技能。
optionExplanations_en: Grinding only the easiest problems just gets you familiar with the page — it never builds the skills a staged, optimization-heavy round needs.
A Medium builds rhythm first, then a Hard forces real optimization thinking — together they match what this round actually demands.
Dropping the timer gives up the biggest resource constraint of the real interview, so the actual pace still feels unfamiliar on the day.
Traditional Easy problems are single-function with no staged flow — that drills a completely different skill set.

q: 补全结构化练习目标：
q_en: Complete the goal of structured practice:
text: 结构化练习的目标是让 CoderPad/HackerRank 式的{{浏览器编辑器}}、{{内置 AI}}和多阶段推进在正式面试前变得熟悉。
why: 陌生的浏览器编辑器和受限 AI 会占用认知带宽，提前练能把这部分预算腾给真正的问题拆解。
why_en: An unfamiliar browser editor and constrained AI eat into your attention, so practicing in advance frees that budget for actual problem solving.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款常见的在线协作编程面试平台，内置浏览器代码编辑器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CoderPad is a common online collaborative coding interview platform with a built-in browser editor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 另一款常用的在线编程测评/面试平台，题目按阶段推进。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HackerRank is another common online coding assessment platform that advances problems in stages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

scenario: 你已经按真实时长完成了三道练习题，但每次都直接跳到下一题，没打开反馈报告。
scenario_en: You have completed three practice problems under real timing, but each time you jumped straight to the next one without opening the feedback report.
q: 这样做主要会让你缺失什么？
q_en: What do you mainly miss by doing this?
options: 不知道自己在 AI 控制、验证、沟通上哪里失控
不知道这道练习题在题库里具体叫什么名字
不知道自己这次练习到底写没写过代码
不知道 AI 助手当时用的是哪个具体模型版本
options_en: You won't know specifically where your AI control, verification, or communication broke down.
You won't know exactly what this practice problem is called in the problem bank.
You won't know for sure whether you wrote any code in this particular practice run.
You won't know exactly which model version the AI assistant was running at the time.
why: 反馈能精确指出你在控制 AI、验证或沟通上的具体弱点；不看反馈，你只能凭感觉猜哪里出了问题。
why_en: Feedback pinpoints exactly where your AI control, verification, or communication broke down; skip it and you're only guessing.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

optionExplanations: 跳过反馈报告，你就失去了唯一能精确定位控制、验证或沟通具体断点的信息来源。
题目叫什么从来不是反馈报告要告诉你的东西，跳过报告也不会漏掉这个。
自己有没有写代码根本不需要靠反馈才知道，这不是反馈缺失带来的损失。
AI 助手用的是哪个模型版本跟你的表现评估无关，反馈报告压根不覆盖这一项。
optionExplanations_en: Skip the feedback report and you lose the one source that pinpoints exactly where your AI control, verification, or communication broke down.
The problem's name was never something the feedback report tells you, so skipping it doesn't cost you that.
You already know whether you wrote code without needing a report to tell you — that's not something feedback loss costs you.
Which model version the AI assistant was running has nothing to do with evaluating your performance, and the report never covers it.

scenario: 你平时能慢慢用 AI 完成题目，但正式面试有固定时长。
scenario_en: You can usually solve problems slowly with AI, but the real interview has a fixed time limit.
q: 练习时应该加入什么约束？
q_en: What constraint should you add during practice?
options: 无限时间直到写出完美答案再停
完全禁止运行任何测试
和真实面试匹配的计时器
只看题目，完全不动手写代码
options_en: Give yourself unlimited time until the answer is perfect.
Ban yourself from running any tests at all.
A timer that matches the real interview length.
Only read the problem and never actually write code.
why: 计时会强迫你在取向、规划、提示和验证之间做真实分配，这个分配是否可行只有掐着表才能暴露。
why_en: A realistic timer forces you to actually split time between orientation, planning, prompting, and verification, and only a clock reveals whether that split works.
whenOtherWins: 第一次熟悉工具时可以先不计时走一遍，之后就该尽快切到真实时间压力。
tradeoff: 计时暴露真实节奏 vs 不计时先求流程完整

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

optionExplanations: 没有截止时间，你永远不会暴露自己在规划和验证上真实能撑多久。
禁止跑测试等于砍掉验证这个评估维度，AI 输出里的隐藏 bug 反而混得过去。
掐着和面试一样长的表，才能看出提示、验证这些环节该怎么在有限时间里分配。
不写代码就没有产出可评审，这不是加约束，是取消了练习本身。
optionExplanations_en: With no deadline, you never find out how your planning and verification actually hold up under real time pressure.
Banning tests removes verification, one of the evaluated skills entirely, letting hidden bugs in AI output slip through unnoticed.
Running a clock as long as the real interview is what actually reveals how to split prompting and verification within limited time.
Without writing any code there's nothing to review — that's not adding a constraint, it's canceling the practice itself.

q: 把根据目标面试选择练习环境的逻辑排好：
q_en: Put the logic for choosing a practice environment by target interview in order:
steps: 优先选择对应格式的练习问题
识别目标面试是开放式还是结构化
在相同约束下计时完成
用反馈修正下一次练习
why: 准备要先确认目标面试的格式，再匹配题目和时间压力，最后用反馈闭环提高。
why_en: Preparation starts by identifying the target interview format, then matches problems and time pressure, and finally closes the loop with feedback.
tradeoff: 先定格式再分配练习资源 vs 不分格式统一刷题
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Target[Target company format] --> Structured{Structured?}
  Structured -->|yes| Browser[Practice browser flow]
  Structured -->|no| IDE[Practice own IDE]
  Browser --> Review[Review feedback]
  IDE --> Review

scenario: 开放式练习让你 clone 仓库到自己电脑，用日常工具和 AI 完整做完一题。
scenario_en: Open-ended practice has you clone a repo to your own machine and solve a full problem with your daily tools and AI.
q: 这类练习重点复现了哪些真实面试条件？（多选）
q_en: Which real interview conditions does this practice mainly recreate? (Select all that apply.)
options: 你自己的机器和编辑器
你日常使用的 AI 工具
从仓库开始构建并按真实时长计时
面试官预先写好的固定内置 AI 助手
options_en: Your own machine and editor.
The AI tools you use day to day.
Starting from the repo and timing yourself realistically.
A fixed built-in AI assistant chosen ahead of time by the interviewer.
why: 固定内置 AI 助手是结构化练习复刻的条件；开放式练的是你自己的机器、工具和真实时限。
why_en: A fixed built-in AI assistant belongs to structured practice; open-ended practice instead recreates your own machine, tools, and real time limit.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

optionExplanations: 你带进面试的就是这台机器和这套编辑器，练习里手感一致，正式当天不会陌生。
日常习惯用的 AI 工具练熟了提示方式，能直接原样搬到面试里用。
从仓库起步加真实计时，复刻的是任务规模和时间压力这两项最容易被低估的变量。
开放式练习里 AI 是你自己挑的，那种不能换、照脚本来的助手其实是结构化沙盒才有的设定。
optionExplanations_en: This is the exact machine and editor you'll bring to the interview, so the feel stays consistent instead of turning unfamiliar on the day.
Practicing with the AI tools you use daily means your prompting habits carry straight over into the real interview.
Starting from the repo with a real timer recreates task scope and time pressure, two variables that are easy to underestimate.
In open-ended practice you pick your own AI — that fixed, can't-swap assistant is actually a structured-sandbox trait.

scenario: 结构化练习让你直接进浏览器沙盒，用平台固定配置的编辑器和 AI 助手按阶段做题。
scenario_en: Structured practice puts you directly into a browser sandbox, using the platform's fixed editor and AI assistant through staged problems.
q: 这类练习重点复现了哪些条件？（多选）
q_en: Which conditions does this practice mainly recreate? (Select all that apply.)
options: 浏览器内编辑器
平台内置 AI 助手
类似 CoderPad/HackerRank 的多阶段流程
完全自由的本地插件环境
options_en: The in-browser editor.
The platform's built-in AI assistant.
A staged flow similar to CoderPad or HackerRank.
A completely free local plugin environment.
why: 结构化练习复刻平台约束，价值在于适应受限编辑器和固定 AI，而不是强化本地插件工作流。
why_en: Structured practice recreates platform constraints, so its value is adapting to a limited editor and fixed AI, not reinforcing your local plugin setup.

termDefinitions.meaning: 一款常见的在线协作编程面试平台，内置浏览器代码编辑器。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: CoderPad is a common online collaborative coding interview platform with a built-in browser editor.

termDefinitions.meaning: 另一款常用的在线编程测评/面试平台，题目按阶段推进。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: HackerRank is another common online coding assessment platform that advances problems in stages.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

termDefinitions.meaning: 集成开发环境，也就是你日常写代码用的编辑器软件，例如 VS Code。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An IDE is the integrated development environment, the editor software you normally write code in, like VS Code.

optionExplanations: 浏览器编辑器的手感和本地 IDE 不一样，提前摸熟能省掉正式面试当天的适应成本。
内置 AI 能力和提示方式都固定死了，练的就是怎么在这个限制下把话说清楚。
按阶段推题要求你按顺序管理时间和优先级，这套节奏得提前练才不生疏。
本地插件配置在结构化沙盒里根本用不上，这条属于开放式练习复刻的条件。
optionExplanations_en: The browser editor feels different from a local IDE, so getting used to it in advance saves adjustment time on the real day.
The built-in AI's capability and prompting style are fixed, so practice is really about phrasing clearly within that limit.
Working through staged problems means managing time and priority in a set order, a rhythm that needs rehearsing beforehand.
Your local plugin setup simply isn't available inside the structured sandbox — that's what open-ended practice recreates instead.

q: 开放式练习和结构化练习的核心区别是什么？
q_en: What is the core difference between open-ended and structured practice?
scenario: 你要挑练习通道：目标面试可能让你屏共自己的 IDE，也可能把你锁进平台浏览器沙盒。
scenario_en: You're picking a practice track: the interview may let you screen-share your own IDE, or lock you into the platform's browser sandbox.
options: 开放式用自己工具，结构化用平台内置工具
开放式不需要 AI，结构化不能写代码
开放式没有时间限制，结构化没有反馈
两者完全一样
options_en: Open-ended uses your own tools, structured uses the platform's built-in tools.
Open-ended doesn't need AI at all, and structured doesn't let you write code.
Open-ended has no time limit, and structured gives no feedback.
The two are completely identical.
why: 两条通道的分界在于工具提供方：开放式用你自己的编辑器和 AI，结构化用平台锁定的浏览器沙盒和内置 AI。
why_en: The core difference is who provides the tools: open-ended uses your own editor and AI, while structured uses the platform's locked-down browser sandbox and built-in AI.
tradeoff: 复刻自带工具的真实工作流 vs 复刻平台锁定的受限环境

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

optionExplanations: 谁提供工具是真正的分界线，这条决定了你练习时该复刻自己的环境还是平台的环境。
两条通道其实都要写代码、都用得上 AI，说其中一条不需要 AI 是错的。
两条通道都设了计时和反馈机制，说哪一条没有时限或没有反馈是错的。
如果两者真的完全一样，平台压根没必要拆成两条练习通道。
optionExplanations_en: Who supplies the tools is the real dividing line, and it decides whether practice should recreate your own setup or the platform's.
Both tracks actually involve writing code and using AI — claiming one skips AI entirely is wrong.
Both tracks come with timing and feedback built in — claiming either one lacks a limit or feedback is wrong.
If the two were truly identical, there'd be no reason for the platform to split practice into two separate tracks.

scenario: 练习反馈说你代码完成了，但 AI 聊天显示你多次接受了无法解释的实现。
scenario_en: Your practice feedback says the code was completed, but the AI chat shows you repeatedly accepted implementations you could not explain.
q: 下一轮练习最该改什么？
q_en: What should you change most in the next practice round?
options: 练习每次 AI 输出后，公开复述并解释关键实现逻辑
换更简单的题目，跳过阅读 AI 生成的代码
为了赶时间练完整套题，直接停用所有单元测试和校验
把精力全部放在缩短点击提交按钮的反应时间上
options_en: After every AI output, practice restating and explaining the key implementation logic out loud.
Switch to easier problems and skip reading the AI-generated code.
To rush through the whole problem set, turn off all unit tests and checks entirely.
Put all your effort into shaving milliseconds off how fast you click submit.
why: 反馈显示的是控制力缺口：能出代码不等于你在掌控实现；下一轮要练成每次输出后立刻复述解释。
why_en: The feedback points to a control gap, since finishing the code isn't the same as owning it, so next time practice narrating and explaining every AI output immediately.
whenOtherWins: 如果反馈主要是算法思路选错，就该回去补相关算法模式，而不是只练讲解习惯。
tradeoff: 每次输出后立即复述解释 vs 全盘接受不追问
codeSample:
After each AI output, say out loud:
1. What this code does: ...
2. Why I accept or reject it: ...
3. One thing I'd verify before moving on: ...

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

optionExplanations: 把复述解释变成每次 AI 输出后的固定动作，练出来的是你能不能对任何一段代码说清它在做什么。
换更简单的题目回避了真正的问题：你现在还是没练成解释已有输出的能力。
停掉单元测试后，连一段解释不清的实现是否正确都没法验证，风险反而更大。
提交更快只是速度指标，证明不了你理解了 AI 写出来的东西。
optionExplanations_en: Making restate-and-explain a fixed step after every AI output trains whether you can actually narrate what any piece of code does.
Switching to an easier problem dodges the real gap — you still haven't built the skill of explaining output you already have.
Turning off unit tests means you can't even check correctness for an implementation you can't explain, which raises the risk.
Submitting faster is just a speed metric — it proves nothing about whether you actually understood what the AI wrote.

q: 补全准备原则：
q_en: Complete the preparation principle:
text: 准备 AI 编码面试不要只读内容；要在{{真实约束}}下练习，提交{{代码和聊天}}，再用{{反馈}}调整。
why: 只读内容学不到双线沟通和验证的节奏；在真实约束下练、把代码和聊天都交出去复盘，才能把知识变成能带上考场的工作流。
why_en: Reading alone can't teach the dual-conversation rhythm; only practicing under real constraints and reviewing both code and chat turns knowledge into an interview-day workflow.
diagram:
flowchart LR
  Format[Match format] --> Timebox[Use timer]
  Timebox --> Build[Build real solution]
  Build --> Feedback[Study feedback]
  Feedback --> Repeat[Repeat deliberately]

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

scenario: 练习题库里是 Battleship、Maze Solver、Task Scheduler、Kitchen Orders 这类题：都是模拟/状态机/图搜索式的工程题，带仓库脚手架，而不是单函数的 LeetCode 算法谜题。
scenario_en: The problem bank lists Battleship, Maze Solver, Task Scheduler, and Kitchen Orders — simulation, state-machine, and graph-search engineering problems with a repo scaffold, not single-function LeetCode puzzles.
q: 这类题库主要训练的是哪种能力？
q_en: Which skill does this problem bank mainly train?
options: 把模糊规格拆成规则、状态和边界，再增量验证
背熟经典算法模板，靠模式识别直接套用现成解法
把单函数的时间复杂度压到理论最优水平
记住常见数据结构 API 的调用语法和参数顺序
options_en: Break a fuzzy spec into rules, state, and edges, then verify incrementally.
Memorize classic algorithm templates and pattern-match a known solution onto the problem.
Optimize a single function's time complexity to the theoretical best.
Memorize the call syntax and argument order of common data-structure APIs.
why: 这些是模拟/状态机/图搜索类工程题，规格是模糊的，考的是把它拆成规则和边界再逐块验证；代价是没有现成模板可背，每题都得重新建模。
why_en: These are simulation and state-machine problems with fuzzy specs, so they test decomposing them into rules and edges and verifying piece by piece — the cost is there's no template to memorize, you re-model each one.
tradeoff: 工程模拟题练需求拆解+增量验证 vs LeetCode 算法题练背模板+模式识别

termDefinitions.meaning: 一个常见的算法刷题网站，题目多是单函数、无 AI 辅助的算法谜题。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: LeetCode is a common algorithm-practice site whose problems are mostly single-function puzzles with no AI assistance.

termDefinitions.meaning: 应用程序编程接口，这里指数据结构或库对外暴露的调用方法和参数。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: An API is the application programming interface — the callable methods and parameters a data structure or library exposes.

termDefinitions.meaning: 人工智能，这里指面试和练习中辅助你写代码的编程助手模型。
termDefinitions.meaningEn: AI here means the coding-assistant model that helps you write code during practice and interviews.

optionExplanations: 规格是模糊的，你得先拆出规则、状态和边界，再一块块写、一块块验证。
背模板在 LeetCode 单函数谜题上管用，但这些模拟题没有现成模板，套不上去。
把复杂度压到最优是算法题的目标；模拟题的难点在正确建模，不在省复杂度。
记 API 语法是基础功；这些题考的是把需求翻译成实现，不是背调用格式。
optionExplanations_en: The spec is fuzzy, so you first extract rules, state, and edges, then build and verify one piece at a time.
Template memorization works on LeetCode single-function puzzles, but these simulation problems have no ready template to fit.
Squeezing complexity to optimal is an algorithm-puzzle goal; the hard part here is correct modeling, not saving complexity.
Memorizing API syntax is table stakes; these problems test translating requirements into an implementation, not recalling call formats.
